messages:
SRE Bot: Paging oncall: Incident 7261 — spike in 5xx for requests routed to dedicated pool 'ded-acme-prod' (customer: AcmeCorp, VPC). Initial alert at 1763647200. @Maia please pick up :rotating_light:
Maia (oncall): I'm on it. Observing increased error rate from 3:22 -> 3:24 UTC. TL;DR looks like route mismatch to a misconfigured backend.
Jamie L.: Is this only AcmeCorp? Any signs of cross-tenant traffic or data leakage?
Priya K.: We're seeing elevated rejects from the routing layer. Logs show requests with X-Tenant: acme-prod hitting nodes in the shared egress group briefly. Need a quick trace of routing table changes.
Omar R.: I pulled the control plane audit: there was an automated rollout to route-policy service at 1763647125, change id rp-2026-03-09-34. It touched rules for dedicated pools - probable regressive rule.
Maia (oncall): Running quick query on router logs:
```
# grep "ded-acme-prod" /var/log/router/2026-03-09.log | tail -n 20
2026-03-09T03:23:11Z GET /v1/generate tenant=acme-prod route=ded-acme-prod -> backend=ded-acme-node-3 status=500
2026-03-09T03:23:11Z GET /v1/generate tenant=acme-prod route=shared-pool -> backend=shared-node-9 status=200
```
Maia (oncall): See two different backends used for same tenant. That suggests routing policy permitted fallback to shared pool.
Jamie L.: That's bad for isolation even if it's only erroring. Prioritize mitigation: can we pin AcmeCorp's tenant route to dedicated pool and disable fallback?
Omar R.: Applying temporary policy rollback now (rp-2026-03-09-34 -> rollback). Command:
```
controlplane apply --rollback rp-2026-03-09-34 --dry-run=false
```
Omar R.: Rollback submitted, awaiting acceptance by control plane. Should be effective in ~30s.
Priya K.: Also toggling strict-tenant-isolation on routing agent for AcmeCorp to prevent any cross-pool fallback. Patch:
```
curl -X POST https://router-admin.local/tenants/acme-prod/isolation -d '{"strict": true}'
```
Priya K.: Patch applied.
Maia (oncall): Post-rollback metrics: 30s after rollback error rate reduced ~80%. No alerts from other tenants so far.
Jamie L.: Good. We need to confirm there was no data exposure. SecBot, can you run an access correlation for requests that hit shared-node-9?
SecBot: Running correlation scan for tenant header overlaps between 03:22:00 and 03:24:30 UTC. This may take ~2m.
Omar R.: While SecBot runs, capturing KV-cache access patterns. If KV keys are namespaced by tenant ID then exposure risk is small.
Priya K.: Quick check: cache keys include tenant prefix for embeddings and KV. Example key: `acme-prod::ctx::user-abcdef`. So raw cross-tenant data reads are unlikely, but logs and ephemeral memory could have mixed traces.
SecBot: Scan complete. No records of cross-tenant response bodies returned to other tenants. Found 12 routed requests that attempted fallback to shared pool; all resulted in 500s. No successful responses from shared pool for acme requests.
Maia (oncall): Summary so far: rollback and strict isolation applied, 5xx rate returning to baseline, no confirmed data leakage.
Jamie L.: Actions: 1) keep strict isolation for 24h, 2) run deeper memory and buffer inspection on shared-node-9, 3) check deployment automation that changed rp-2026-03-09-34, 4) customer comms draft. Assign owners.
Omar R.: I'll handle (2) memory/buffer scans and (3) deployment pipeline audit.
Priya K.: I'll own (1) and monitor metrics + create alert to detect any future fallback activity.
Maia (oncall): I'll draft comms and wait for security sign-off.
SecBot: Note: opened SEC-INV-1122 for post-incident forensic. Tags: tenant-isolation, routing, dedicated-pool.
Jamie L.: For the postmortem include: timeline, root cause (regressive route-policy change allowing fallback), immediate mitigations (rollback + strict flag), verification steps (Sec scan + memory checks), and follow-ups (deploy gating, circuit-breakers).
Maia (oncall): Quick note for customers: "We detected and mitigated an infrastructure routing regression affecting AcmeCorp's dedicated pool. No evidence of successful cross-tenant data exposure; services restored. We'll follow up with detailed forensic summary." I'll send once Sec sign-off.
Omar R.: Memory scan: no tenant data found in freed buffers on shared-node-9. KV namespace checks OK. Still running heap dump analysis, ETA 45m.
Priya K.: Monitoring looks stable for 10m. Reopening monitoring dashboard to keep eyes on it.
Jamie L.: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this thread open for postmortem inputs. If anyone finds anything that contradicts SecBot's scan, ping immediately. :thumbsup:
SecBot: For the record, SEC-INV-1122 assigned to Priya K., Omar R., and Maia.
Maia (oncall): Handoff to next oncall in 2h; will include status and actions in handoff.
Maia (oncall): Ending live mitigation. Last check at 1763647650 - incident stabilized.
